title: Week of September 12, 2026
description:
BENDY: Thursday night we make honey sesame chicken, and Friday I don't cook at all. Same chicken, chopped cold into a salad, and it tastes like a different dinner.

BUB: So Friday is just Thursday in a bowl.

BENDY: Friday is Thursday with a crunch. That's the whole trick this week.

BUB: What do we do today?

BENDY: Freezer, first. Two pork tenderloins and the chicken thighs come out and go in the fridge. Not the counter.

BUB: Why not the counter?

BENDY: Because a tenderloin thaws from the outside in, and the outside sits warm for hours. Fridge is slower and safer.

BENDY: Tonight I rub the pork — salt, garlic powder, smoked paprika, dried thyme, a spoon of brown sugar — and wrap it tight. Twenty-four hours and the salt gets all the way in.

BENDY: Then two heads of cauliflower into the food processor. Pulse, don't puree. Half in a bag for Monday, half for Thursday.

BUB: Can I do the buttons?

BENDY: You can do the buttons. Also today: whisk the sesame sauce in a jar — honey, soy, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger — and stem the kale for Wednesday.

BENDY: Sunday is Traeger Herb-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Apples. I run it at 400 and pull it at 145 in the thick end.

BUB: What if you leave it longer?

BENDY: Then it's 160 and it eats like a pencil eraser. Pull at 145, rest ten minutes, slice. And the Brussels go cut-side down so they blister instead of steaming. I'm throwing in a delicata squash too, seeds out, half-moons, skin on.
